Magnetic field lines:

__
 
• A magnetic field line is an imaginary line such that tangent to it at any point gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point in space.
 
• Magnetic field lines are drawn to represent the magnetic fields.
 
• Magnetic field lines can be drawn with the help of a magnetic compass.
 
• Magnetic field lines are also called magnetic lines of force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Properties of magnetic field lines:

 
• The magnetic field lines of a magnet (or a solenoid) form continuous closed loops.
 
• The magnetic field lines start from the north pole and end on a south pole outside the magnet. Inside the magnet, the magnetic field lines start from the south pole and end on the north pole.
 
• The tangent to the field line at a given point represents the direction of the net magnetic field B at that point.
 
• The larger the number of field lines crossing per unit area, the stronger is the magnitude of the magnetic field B.
 
• The magnetic field lines do not intersect with each other if they did, there will be two directions of the magnetic field at that point which is not possible.

dfrac{AD}{DB} = dfrac{AE}{EC}

questions.question: Kamal is now four times as old as his son now is. After 18 years his son will be half as old as Kamal would then be. Find the present age (in years) of the son.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Kamal is now four times as old as his son now is. After 18 years his son will be half as old as Kamal would then be.

**Formula used:**

Let the present age of Kamal's son be x years.

Therefore, the present age of Kamal = 4x years.

After 18 years:

Kamal's age = 4x + 18

Son's age = x + 18

According to the given condition:

x + 18 = 1/2 (4x + 18)

**Calculation:**

x + 18 = 1/2 (4x + 18)

⇒ 2(x + 18) = 4x + 18

⇒ 2x + 36 = 4x + 18

⇒ 36 - 18 = 4x - 2x

⇒ 18 = 2x

⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

• The Easter lily, a symbol of the resurrection in Western Christianity, traditionally decorates the chancel area of churches on Easter Day and throughout the Eastertide season.
 
• Additional customs include egg hunting, the Easter Bunny, and Easter parades.

__
 
• A concave mirror is a type of curved mirror where the reflective surface bulges inward.
 
• When light rays that are initially parallel to the principal axis reflect off the surface, they converge at a point known as the focal point.

__

Thus both can be delivered via pipelines in specific contexts. *(Statement 2: **Correct (context-dependent)**)*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In cost theory, the point where the marginal cost curve intersects the average cost curve at its minimum indicates optimal production efficiency.
 
• The intersection of LRMC and LRAC at the minimum point of LRAC signals the firm's most efficient scale in the long run.
 
• This concept is essential in understanding cost minimization and firm behavior over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Long Run Marginal Cost (LRMC) and Long Run Average Cost (LRAC):

 
 
• The long run marginal cost (LRMC) curve represents the additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of output in the long run.
 
• The long run average cost (LRAC) curve reflects the per-unit cost of production when all inputs are variable in the long run.
 
• The LRMC curve always intersects the LRAC curve at the minimum point of the LRAC curve, indicating the point of optimal efficiency.
 
• At this point, the cost of producing an additional unit equals the average cost, which means the firm is operating at the most efficient scale of production.
 
• The short run marginal cost (SRMC) curve does pass through the minimum point of the short run average cost (SRAC) curve, indicating the optimal output level in the short run.
 
• The short run marginal cost curve does not necessarily relate to the upward-rising portion of the long run average cost curve.
 
• The short run average cost curve may not necessarily touch the minimum point of the long run average cost curve.

questions.question: Redox reaction is the reaction in which ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Redox reaction-

__
 
• A redox (reduction-oxidation) reaction is a type of chemical reaction that involves the transfer of electrons between species.
 
• It consists of two simultaneous processes: reduction and oxidation.
 
 
• Reduction: In a redox reaction, reduction refers to the gain of electrons by a species. During reduction, the oxidation state of the species decreases, indicating a decrease in its positive charge or an increase in its negative charge.
 
• Oxidation: Oxidation, on the other hand, involves the loss of electrons by a species. It leads to an increase in the oxidation state of the species, indicating an increase in its positive charge or a decrease in its negative charge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Example of redox reaction-

 
• MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2

 
 
• ​MnO2 is manganese dioxide, and HCl is hydrochloric acid.
 
• In this reaction, manganese dioxide (MnO2) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl) to produce manganese(II) chloride (MnCl2), water (H2O), and chlorine gas (Cl2).
 
• MnO2 acts as the oxidizing agent, while HCl acts as the reducing agent.
 
• The manganese dioxide undergoes reduction, meaning it gains electrons. It is reduced from an oxidation state of +4 in MnO2 to +2 in MnCl2.
 
• The hydrochloric acid undergoes oxidation, meaning it loses electrons. The chlorine atoms in HCl are oxidized from an oxidation state of -1 to 0 in Cl2.
 
• As a result of the reaction, two hydrogen atoms from the hydrochloric acid combine with one oxygen atom from the manganese dioxide to form water (H2O).
 
• Simultaneously, the remaining chlorine atoms from the hydrochloric acid combine to form chlorine gas (Cl2).
 
• Overall, the reaction involves the transfer of electrons from manganese dioxide to hydrochloric acid, resulting in the formation of new compounds and the liberation of chlorine gas.

The correct answer is __**Double displacement and precipitation reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Double displacement **

 
 
• Double displacement reaction occurs between ionic compounds.
 
• In a double displacement reaction, two ionic compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds.
 
• The reaction takes place in aqueous solutions or in the molten state.
 
• The products of the reaction are usually a precipitate, water, or a gas.
 
• Ionic compounds are composed of positively charged metal ions and negatively charged non-metal ions, and they dissociate into their ions in water or in the molten state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation reactions**

 
 
• Precipitation reactions occur when two aqueous solutions containing soluble salts are mixed, and the resulting mixture leads to the formation of an insoluble solid product. This insoluble solid is called a precipitate.
 
• In this specific reaction:
 
• Reactants:
 
• Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) is dissolved in water (aq)
 
• Calcium chloride (CaCl2) is also dissolved in water (aq)
 
• Products:
 
• Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is formed as a solid precipitate (s).
 
• Sodium chloride (NaCl) remains dissolved in water (aq).
 
• The driving force behind this reaction is the formation of the insoluble calcium carbonate. When the solutions of sodium carbonate and calcium chloride are mixed, the calcium ions (Ca2+) from calcium chloride combine with the carbonate ions (CO3²-) from sodium carbonate to form calcium carbonate, which is insoluble in water and thus precipitates out of the solution.

questions.question: The sum of the ages of 4 boys born at intervals of 5 years each is 42 years. What is the age of the youngest boy?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of the ages of 4 boys born at intervals of 5 years each is 42 years.

**Formula used:**

Let the age of the youngest boy be x years.

The ages of the other boys will be: x + 5, x + 10, and x + 15 years.

**Calculation:**

Sum of ages = x + (x + 5) + (x + 10) + (x + 15) = 42

⇒ x + x + 5 + x + 10 + x + 15 = 42

⇒ 4x + 30 = 42

⇒ 4x = 42 - 30

⇒ 4x = 12

⇒ x = 12/4

⇒ x = 3

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

• When plants are kept in a dark room for three days, they undergo significant changes due to the lack of sunlight, which is crucial for their survival and growth. Here's what happens:
 
• Photosynthesis Stops: Plants rely on sunlight to perform photosynthesis, the process of converting light energy into chemical energy (glucose). In the absence of light, photosynthesis ceases. This means the plant can no longer produce its own food.

• Withering and Death: If the plant is kept in the dark for an extended period, it will eventually exhaust its stored energy reserves and die.

__
 
• Some fish breathe by gulping water through their mouths. This is how they extract the oxygen they need to survive underwater.
 
• **Water Intake:** The fish opens its mouth and takes in a mouthful of water.
 
• **Gill Passage:** The water then passes over the gills, which are located on either side of the fish's head.
 
• **Oxygen Extraction: **The gills, which are composed of delicate, feathery structures, are richly supplied with blood vessels. As the water flows over the gills, oxygen dissolved in the water diffuses into the bloodstream of the fish.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide Release:** Simultaneously, carbon dioxide, a waste product of the fish's metabolism, diffuses from the blood into the water.
 
• **Water Expulsion:** Finally, the water, now depleted of oxygen and enriched with carbon dioxide, is expelled from the fish's body through the gill slits.
 
• This process of water intake, oxygen extraction, and carbon dioxide release is a continuous cycle that allows fish to obtain the oxygen they need for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gills are the primary respiratory organs of fish. They are highly specialized structures that maximize the efficiency of gas exchange.
 
• Countercurrent Exchange: The flow of water over the gills and the flow of blood within the gill filaments are in opposite directions. This countercurrent exchange mechanism ensures that the blood is always exposed to water with a higher oxygen concentration, maximizing the amount of oxygen that can be absorbed.
 
• Efficiency: Fish gills are incredibly efficient at extracting oxygen from water. This is crucial because the concentration of dissolved oxygen in water is much lower than the concentration of oxygen in air.

• Fundamental Duties:__
 
• 
 
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• They are listed in Part IVA under Article 51A.
 
• These duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
 
• Currently, there are 11 Fundamental Duties, but originally there were 10.
 
 
 
• Swaran Singh Committee:
 
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was appointed by the Government of India in 1976.
 
• The committee was headed by Swaran Singh, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.
 
• The main objective of the committee was to make recommendations for the incorporation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
• Based on its recommendations, the 42nd Amendment Act was enacted, which added the Fundamental Duties to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• 42nd Amendment Act, 1976:
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging changes to the Constitution.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period imposed by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• Besides adding Fundamental Duties, it also brought changes to various parts of the Constitution, including the Preamble and the structure of the judiciary.
 
• Some of the provisions introduced by the 42nd Amendment were later modified or repealed by subsequent amendments.

questions.question: If a number is divisible by 4, then which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The unit place in the number is 0.
The sum of the digits in the number is divisible by 4.
The number formed by its last two digit is divisible by 4.
The number will be divisible by 2 and 6.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

If a number is divisible by 4, then which of the following statements is true?

**Formula used:**

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

**Calculation:**

If the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4, then the entire number is divisible by 4.

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
